facts.raw_span: a 17-year history of migraine headaches
a visual aura of gray-white spots followed by pain behind the right eye radiating to the right frontal, temporal, and suboccipital regions
3 to 4 severe migraines per month lasting 3 to 7 days
relief only from sumatriptan after trials of acetaminophen, ibuprofen, rizatriptan, methylprednisolone, prednisone, and dexamethasone failed
a right orbital and medial cheek headache radiating to the right lateral jaw, ear, and down the right suboccipital region
treatment with ketorolac, rizatriptan, and a 7-day dexamethasone taper failed to resolve her symptoms
naratriptan, prochlorperazine, acetaminophen, ibuprofen, and diphenhydramine without improvement
Brain magnetic resonance imaging was unremarkable
an ultrasound-guided right sphenopalatine ganglion block with 4 mL of bupivacaine 0.25% and 1 mL of dexamethasone 4 mg/mL
this treatment also failed to resolve her symptoms

concepts.why: The patient has a 17-year history of migraine headaches and experiences a visual aura of gray-white spots followed by pain behind the right eye.
The patient experiences 3 to 4 severe migraines per month lasting 3 to 7 days and has tried various treatments without relief.
The patient experiences a prolonged migraine lasting more than 3 days and has tried various treatments without relief.
The patient underwent an ultrasound-guided right sphenopalatine ganglion block with 4 mL of bupivacaine 0.25% and 1 mL of dexamethasone 4 mg/mL, but this treatment failed to resolve her symptoms.
The patient has tried various medications, including sumatriptan, acetaminophen, ibuprofen, rizatriptan, methylprednisolone, prednisone, and dexamethasone, without relief.
The patient experiences a new type of headache that is daily and persistent, and brain magnetic resonance imaging was unremarkable.
The patient experiences a continuous headache on one side of the head, and the sphenopalatine ganglion block failed to resolve her symptoms.
The patient experiences a severe headache on one side of the head, and the treatments tried have failed to resolve her symptoms.
The patient experiences a headache with autonomic features, such as a visual aura, and the treatments tried have failed to resolve her symptoms.
The patient experiences a headache that is referred from the cervical spine, and the sphenopalatine ganglion block failed to resolve her symptoms.

rationales.F01: Long history of migraine headaches suggests chronic condition
rationales.F02: Visual aura is a characteristic feature of migraine with aura
rationales.F03: Frequency and duration of migraines suggest chronic migraine
rationales.F04: Failure of multiple treatments suggests medication-overuse headache
rationales.F05: Location and radiation of pain suggest hemicrania continua or cervicogenic headache
rationales.F09: Sphenopalatine ganglion block is a treatment for various headache disorders
rationales.F10: Failure of sphenopalatine ganglion block suggests refractory condition

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's history of frequent and severe migraines, along with the recent development of a prolonged and refractory headache, supports the diagnosis of Status migrainosus, which is characterized by a migraine that lasts more than 72 hours.
